rules.specification: Assess whether the title identifies the page's subject or purpose. The page supplies no title-length requirement.
rules.violation_condition: A page title is vague or misleading about the page's subject or purpose.
when: When assessing a web page's title.
rules.why: G-1: this is a specific textual requirement within the accessibility section.

rules.quote: Describe the topics or the following section in the headings.
rules.violation_condition: A heading does not describe the topic or section it introduces.
when: When a heading introduces a topic or section.
rules.why: G-1: descriptive heading wording is a distinct check from the organisation of headings.

rules.quote: To group content into topics or connected ideas, prioritised by level of importance, use a hierarchical structure.
rules.violation_condition: Content intended to group and prioritise topics or connected ideas lacks a hierarchy representing those relationships.
when: When grouping content into topics or connected ideas prioritised by importance.
rules.why: G-1: retain the specific hierarchy requirement rather than an additional parent-level structure rule.

rules.quote: To present a sequence of steps or events, use a sequential structure.
rules.violation_condition: Steps or events are arranged in a way that does not preserve the sequence needed to follow the process or progression.
when: When presenting a sequence of steps or events.
rules.why: G-1: the required ordering of steps or events is a specific structural check.

rules.quote: To guide people from beginning to end, use a narrative structure.
rules.specification: This applies to content intended to tell an entire story, as explained by the following sentences. Assess narrative progression, not a mandatory chronological ordering.
rules.violation_condition: Content intended to tell an entire story lacks a narrative progression carrying the reader through it.
when: When the content is intended to guide people through an entire story from beginning to end.
rules.why: G-1: retain the specific narrative requirement; the following explanation establishes its storytelling context.

rules.specification: Assess convention against the content type and consistency against the organisation established in the document. The page provides no exhaustive list of acceptable structures.
rules.violation_condition: Content has an unconventional structure or inconsistent organisation that makes its arrangement unpredictable.
rules.why: The instruction identifies a predictability check, distinct from choosing a structure for a particular content purpose.

covers.quote: Organise content in a clear order using section headings.

rules.quote: Use a logical hierarchy or sequential steps for headings.
rules.specification: Assess the conceptual hierarchy or sequence expressed by the headings. This does not establish a separate rule about HTML heading-level syntax.
rules.violation_condition: The headings express an illogical hierarchy or place sequential steps in an illogical order.
when: When organising content with headings.
Either a logical hierarchy or sequential steps can satisfy the instruction.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate the earlier clear-order instruction here; heading wording and topical grouping remain separate checks.

rules.quote: Write a topic sentence for each paragraph.
rules.violation_condition: A paragraph has no topic sentence identifying its main idea.
when: When assessing prose paragraphs.
rules.why: G-1: this is a specific paragraph-level check under the broader scanning section.

rules.quote: Display important information in lists, callout boxes, tables and illustrations.
rules.specification: Treat the named formats as available ways to display important information, not a requirement to repeat every important point in all four formats. Importance depends on the content and user purpose.
rules.violation_condition: Important information is left only in ordinary running prose rather than displayed in a list, callout box, table or illustration.
when: When presenting important information.
rules.why: G-2: the named presentation forms are alternatives within one information-presentation check.

rules.quote: Structure your content by writing about one idea at a time:
rules.specification: Interpret this as developing ideas in turn rather than repeatedly switching between unfinished ideas. It does not specify one idea per sentence or per paragraph.
rules.violation_condition: The development of separate ideas is interleaved, with the text repeatedly leaving an unfinished idea to develop another and then returning to it.
when: When developing multiple ideas in content.
rules.why: The lead-in states a textual property distinct from the following checks on priority, grouping, length and order.

rules.quote: Start with the most important idea first.
rules.specification: Assess the opening idea of the content being structured. Importance is judged against the user's purpose; the page gives no mechanical ranking or instruction to apply this separately to every paragraph.
rules.violation_condition: Less important ideas precede the most important idea at the start of the content.
when: When arranging the ideas in content.
rules.why: This checks the placement of the leading idea, rather than the existence of a hierarchy or topical grouping.

rules.violation_condition: Related ideas are not collected into a topical group under a heading.
when: When organising related ideas in content.
rules.why: This checks topical grouping under headings, separately from heading wording and hierarchy.

rules.specification: The page does not define short. A paragraph-length criterion needs reviewer agreement; no word or sentence threshold is inferred here.
rules.violation_condition: Ideas are packed into an overlong paragraph rather than divided into short paragraphs.
when: When presenting ideas in prose paragraphs.
rules.why: E-4: retain the paragraph-length requirement without inventing a numerical definition of short.

rules.quote: Make sure ideas flow from one paragraph to the next.
rules.specification: Assess whether successive paragraphs have an intelligible progression of ideas. Explicit transition words are not required when the relationship is already clear.
rules.violation_condition: Successive paragraphs have an incoherent progression or an abrupt, unexplained jump between ideas.
when: When content contains successive paragraphs.
rules.why: This checks progression between paragraphs, distinct from the order of sentences within a paragraph.

rules.quote: Use a logical order for sentences.
rules.specification: Assess whether sentence order supports the progression and dependencies of the ideas. Several different orders may be logical.
rules.violation_condition: The order of sentences disrupts the logical progression of the ideas.
when: When arranging multiple sentences in prose.
rules.why: This is the sentence-order check, not a second finding for paragraph-to-paragraph flow.
